rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause requirement (Civil Code 1946.2)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential property for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written termination notice. rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Rental property owners and their agents may not pay for or use the services of a coordinator, meaning anyone operating algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function. Coordinators may not facilitate agreements that restrict competition. No person may engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination or perform a coordinating function. Violations are violations of the New Jersey Antitrust Act.

Residential dwelling units are any house, apartment, accessory unit or other unit intended as a primary residence in the State.
rules.exemptions: Residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. Algorithmic devices exclude spreadsheets that operate without artificial intelligence and require human analysis, and databases that only use an algorithm to query unprocessed stored data. Coordinating functions exclude: use of competitively sensitive information solely for research, statistical analysis or testing not used to set or recommend lease terms; free public rent estimates; real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms that do not set or recommend prices or collect competitively sensitive information for that purpose; and government entities setting or limiting rents through affordability controls. rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA)
rules.requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability.

coverage_conditions.text: All landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston, including buyers of foreclosed properties as to former owners and tenants.

rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility, and residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement. The Notice of
Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to
Quit.
rules.penalty: Enforced by the Inspectional Services Department: warning for a 1st offense; $300 per day for 2nd and subsequent offenses. A violation does not halt the eviction process. The requirements cannot be waived, and lease terms purporting to waive them are void.
rules.effective_date_phrase: The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy - criminal history
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not use a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests or convictions and must consider applicants case by case. When deciding housing eligibility or eviction, they may not consider arrests that did not result in conviction, convictions subject to judicial relief such as expungement or sealing, juvenile records, or a conviction more than 5 years old.

rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers and rental agents may not discriminate in viewing or renting an apartment or in terms and conditions of tenancy based on protected categories, including source of income (which includes Section 8 and public benefits).
